edits.content:
## Reasoning line (required before the answer tags)
Write ONE line first: `ASKS = <person / category noun / thing / place / word>; BARE = <final answer>; FORM = <inflection>`.
- ASKS: the type named by the clue's pronoun or noun (see Rule 2). Reject any candidate of another type, or one that already appears in the clue. BARE: apply the DELETE-CLUE-WORDS TEST (Rule 4) and also drop type words the passages attach (River, Island, Museum, House, Party, Company, series), unless the head-noun exception applies. FORM: if the clue defines a word ('term for FOLLOWING a winding course'), answer in the inflection the definition uses (-ing -> 'Meandering'), not the base headword.
- A verbatim archive answer (Rule 3) is copied as printed and skips the BARE strike.

edits.target: - Ask: what category is the answer (country, person, vitamin, object, band), and what member of that category fits all the clue details?
edits.content:
- CLASS TEST: read the noun after 'this' (with its adjectives) as the class the answer must belong to, and check that your candidate is an instance of that class. 'the 1815 battle in this Belgian town' -> the town, not 'Battle of ...'. 'this strong acid used in car batteries' -> an acid, not a base or other chemical. 'The energy from this' / 'a product of this' -> the SOURCE or maker, not the energy or product restated.
- OWNER vs ARTIFACT: when the clue describes something a person owns, made or wrote ('Her home in X is now a museum', 'he wrote an explanation of why...', 'her debut'), the answer is the PERSON, as a bare name. Never answer with the museum, house, poem, letter or event that the passages are full of; those are anchors. 'A series/collection on these <things of an era>' -> the plain plural category noun that 'these' stands for, not the name of the series or exhibit.
- BARE DEFINITION (no 'this', e.g. 'A church official who ...'): answer the exact role or class the definition describes, as the plain generic noun the passages gloss it with. Do not drift to a neighbouring role (an assistant, a related product, the most famous brand). After the class is right, strip any word the clue already states.

edits.target: The 'do not repeat clue words' rule is for a separate modifier already stated in the clue ('hasty' + pudding).
edits.content: - ENGLISH FORM OF FOREIGN NAMES: when the clue is in English and uses an English generic type noun for a landmark, building or institution ('this palace', 'this cathedral', 'this bridge'), answer with the standard English form that contains that noun, with a leading 'the' if usage runs that way ('the Pitti Palace', not 'Palazzo Pitti'). If the passages show both forms, choose the English one. Keep the foreign form only when the clue itself uses foreign words or the name has no common English equivalent.

edits.target: Do not choose one that fits only some.
edits.content: - SHARED-PAGE TRAP: retrospectives, Hall of Fame pieces and stat tables print several people's careers side by side, so the most-mentioned name may be the neighbour. Attach each fact to the person it is printed under, and treat the clue's team, league, employer and years as hard constraints. Reject any candidate who never played or served for the team the clue names, even if his name appears in most snippets. Prefer the career-record page whose totals match the clue's numbers exactly, and sanity-check with your own knowledge.

a JSON dump line ("question": "...", "answer": "..."), or flashcard front/back (the answer follows the clue's last words). Copy a parenthesized optional part exactly as the archive prints it ('(First) Last' stays '(First) Last').

edits.target: - Otherwise, build the answer from passages that match several of the clue's details.
edits.content: - Passage TITLES are answer candidates. When a passage's [TLE] is a headword or work title and its [PAR] snippet restates the clue's definition or plot details, the title is the answer. Normalize it: drop disambiguators like '(1956 film)' or '(miniseries)', use the singular of a plural headword (unless Rule 4 keeps the plural), and keep any hyphen or leading 'The' that belongs to the standard name.

edits.target: - 'One of these <role/title>' ('the 14th one of these spiritual leaders') asks for the title or category noun itself (Dalai Lama), not the individual named in the clue.
edits.content: - '<Named actor> played this <role/description>' asks for the CHARACTER played; the actor and year are anchors. Answer with the role's name as the passages give it, even if it is also the film's title. Only a clue whose subject is the pronoun ('She played X...') asks for the actor. A '<year> hit / song that contains the lines "..."' clue asks for the SONG TITLE printed beside the quoted line in lyric passages, not the artist or album.

edits.target: answer with the common English name (Conch).
edits.content: - Etymology clues ('this adjective comes from the Latin for "..."') ask for the ENGLISH word whose dictionary or etymology passages repeat the quoted gloss and the stated part of speech, not the Latin source word or a paraphrase.
